The screenshot visibly shows device time 8:25. This is not treated as generated_at.

The generated metadata strongly captures cinematic brooding and revenge/comeback, but the result terminates after four tracks. The selected tracks emphasize inward-looking melancholy, wounded affect, detachment, and brooding; revenge/comeback is stronger in the metadata than the selections.

The user attests that this result and its paired Revenge in Slow Motion result were generated from the same prompt in immediate succession after navigating back and resubmitting. The outputs differ materially in track count, identities, style distribution, and apparent construction strategy. The cause is unknown.

Despite radically different track construction, both outputs use the title Revenge in Slow Motion and closely similar cinematic-brooding comeback descriptions. High-level semantic interpretation appears more stable than downstream playlist realization. This is not proof of internal architecture.

The two outputs appear to represent very different musical realizations of a nearly identical semantic abstraction: one is intimate, vocal-heavy, melancholy/pop-adjacent and four tracks; the retry is broader across alternative, post-rock, trip-hop, shoegaze, and dark rock/metal-adjacent material and forty tracks.

The four-track result remains a real observed generation, but the immediate forty-track retry weakens strong causal claims such as hard constraint ceiling, candidate scarcity, insufficient catalog, or deterministic refusal to pad. Supported conclusion: one same-prompt generation severely undergenerated while an immediate retry did not.

This paired case may help distinguish prompt-interpretation stability, candidate or retrieval variance, construction or ranking variance, output-length variance, and sequencing variance. No observed variance is attributed to a particular internal Maestro stage.
